items.reasoning: Evaluated under Mode B (Subjective Evaluation), the report fully reproduces the Figure 5 qualitative showcase on doge.png using the released Janus-1.3B checkpoint: it extracts both captions verbatim ("Decoupling Visual Encoding" and "Single Visual Encoder"), contrasts the "muscular" dog with the "more relaxed"/"sitting" dog, and connects them respectively to separating layers/"more efficient and powerful" processing versus processing data as a "single unit." Beyond the original paper's single-prompt showcase, the agent conducts a five-prompt probe with a 14-point critical audit—uncovering missed crying cues, minor self-contradictions, and hallucinated technical glosses—and mechanistically shows on doge.png (Fig. 7b) that the VQ generation encoder destroys caption legibility and collapses comprehension under pathway swapping. Although relying on pretrained weights on CPU rather than training from scratch limits novelty, the critical error analysis and mechanistic verification provide substantially stronger rigor and supporting evidence than the paper's qualitative figure.
